title: Find a boundary
prompt: values is sorted from smallest to largest and may contain repeats. Return the index of the first element that is greater than or equal to target. When every element is smaller, return values.length. The last check allows 40 reads in an array of 100,000.
hints: The answer is a position from 0 to values.length. What should the starting range be?
When the middle element is smaller than target, the answer is to its right. Otherwise the middle itself may be the answer, so keep it in the range.
low = 0, high = values.length. While low < high: if values[middle] < target then low = middle + 1, else high = middle. Return low.
checkLabels: 4 is missing. The first element at least 4 is 5, at index 2.
No element is at least 8, so the answer is the length.
With repeats, the answer is the first of them.
Read no more than 40 of the 100,000 elements.

wrongAnswers.misconception: Returns as soon as it sees an equal element, which may not be the first one.
Finds the first element that is strictly greater than the target.

feedback: Decide what the range means before writing the loop: every position from low to high could still be the answer. Then check the array of three equal numbers by hand.
